liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls the Scarlet, Fire, Estimated, Eyes run the best they've heard, though a fall Centrum Scarlet-Fire rates higher; Reviewer calls this Scarlet>Fire the yardstick for all others, despite coming from 1983 rather than 1977 [19][25][29]
- **Morning Dew** (3 reviews): The soundboard copy has a bad cut in Morning Dew; Morning Dew is long and spirited [18][19][28]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): West L.A. Fadeaway is played in a laid-back version [22]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Ramble On Rose as a draw for fans of that song [24]
- **Maybe You Know** (1 review): Maybe You Know was rarely played, so worth having for collectors [28]
- **Throwing Stones** (1 review): Throwing Stones is nice and tight [20]
- **Baby, You Know How I'm Feelin'** (1 review): Reviewer had never heard this song before; calls it a standout rarity, with Brent praised [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **Maybe You Know**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 6 archived performances [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-13.mtx.seamons.113852.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 165 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd83-04-13.sbd.sacks.1614.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 165 min; rated 4.1/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds good but needs the volume turned up; captures Brent's analog keyboard jams; Soundboard quality is good once the volume is turned up [22][23]
- **gd83-04-13.sbd.lai.23849.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 3.2/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is good but not astonishing; Garcia's guitar is quiet at first, improving as the show goes on; Soundboard has guitars low and vocals prominent, but offers more clarity than the audience version [24][27]
- **gd1983-04-13.162702.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 166 min [6]
- **gd1983-04-13.nak300.andrewf.82876.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 157 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [10]
- **gd83-04-13.horvath-sennheiser.ladner.21921.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 144 min; rated 4.73/5 by 30 [14]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is bright, evenly mixed and free of the muddiness heard on circulating soundboards; Crisp audience recording; Reviewer, a stickler for quality, finds the sound great [18][20][29]
- **gd1983-04-13.138339.SBD.set2.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 11 songs; 105 min [16]

## Around the show

- Reportedly almost impossible for non-university students to get into the show [19]
- Weir's vocals sound hoarse, while Garcia and especially Brent are on target; high-energy show [24]
- The audience version captures the band's overall balance better than the soundboard does [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-13.mtx.seamons.113852.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Jubal H. Seamons using Final Cut Pro (SHN > AIFF > Final Cut > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT) [1]
- **gd83-04-13.sbd.sacks.1614.sbeok.shnf**: source: MSC -> Reel (3 3/4 ips) -> Revox A-77 (reel to reel deck) -> Alesis Masterlink ML-9600 (A/D conversion and CDR mastering) -> CDRs -> EAC -> SHN [2]
- **gd83-04-13.sbd.lai.23849.sbeok.shnf**: source: SDB> CM> C> DAT> CDR [3]
- **gd1983-04-13.162702.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 x Sennheiser 421 mics > unknown mixer > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: Transferred from Jim Vita's master cassettes by Charlie Miller, with a Nakamichi 304 source patching short gaps in Eyes and Drums; Pitch correction was applied with help from Joe B. Jones [6]
- **gd1983-04-13.nak300.andrewf.82876.flac16**: taped by Andrew F; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM-300's (no shotguns) > patched thru one Sony D5 > Marantz PMD-340 > TDK SA-90's. Mics on stand aprx six feet high, set up second or third row up in… [10]. Also: Nakamichi 300 recording that omits the drums; patches come from the Horvath recording (shnid 21921) [10]
- **gd83-04-13.horvath-sennheiser.ladner.21921.sbeok.shnf**: source: MAC(FOB Sennheiser 421)>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN. [14]. Also: Reviewer knew the show only from soundboard copies, where the second set is lower generation than the first; Reviewer lost their tape of the show years ago and is glad to have it back [18][25]
- **gd1983-04-13.138339.SBD.set2.Gastwirt.Miller.Noel.t-flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Set 2 1st gen dbx cassette SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (dbx) > DAT; Charlie Miller [16]. Also: Second-set soundboard transfer by Gastwirt and Miller; the set matches Mark Horvath's front-of-board recording, shnid 21921 [16]

claims.text: Audience recording is bright, evenly mixed and free of the muddiness heard on circulating soundboards
Reviewer knew the show only from soundboard copies, where the second set is lower generation than the first
The soundboard copy has a bad cut in Morning Dew
Reviewer calls the Scarlet, Fire, Estimated, Eyes run the best they've heard, though a fall Centrum Scarlet-Fire rates higher
Morning Dew is long and spirited
Reportedly almost impossible for non-university students to get into the show

claims.song: Baby, You Know How I'm Feelin'
claims.text: Reviewer had never heard this song before; calls it a standout rarity, with Brent praised
Throwing Stones is nice and tight
Crisp audience recording
West L.A. Fadeaway is played in a laid-back version
Soundboard sounds good but needs the volume turned up; captures Brent's analog keyboard jams
Soundboard quality is good once the volume is turned up
Soundboard is good but not astonishing; Garcia's guitar is quiet at first, improving as the show goes on
Weir's vocals sound hoarse, while Garcia and especially Brent are on target; high-energy show
Reviewer singles out Ramble On Rose as a draw for fans of that song
Reviewer calls this Scarlet>Fire the yardstick for all others, despite coming from 1983 rather than 1977
Reviewer lost their tape of the show years ago and is glad to have it back
Soundboard has guitars low and vocals prominent, but offers more clarity than the audience version
The audience version captures the band's overall balance better than the soundboard does
Maybe You Know was rarely played, so worth having for collectors
Reviewer likes Morning Dew emerging from Space
Band teases Fire, noodles around it repeatedly, then lands it with a descending run and cymbal work from the drummers
Reviewer, a stickler for quality, finds the sound great
Transferred from Jim Vita's master cassettes by Charlie Miller, with a Nakamichi 304 source patching short gaps in Eyes and Drums
Pitch correction was applied with help from Joe B. Jones
Nakamichi 300 recording that omits the drums; patches come from the Horvath recording (shnid 21921)
Second-set soundboard transfer by Gastwirt and Miller; the set matches Mark Horvath's front-of-board recording, shnid 21921
This is a matrix recording by Seamons, in 16-bit FLAC
